item.content:encoded:
I love this. I'm a sucker for the more psychological horrors, like SCP-3001, the ones that use emotion to fuck with you. It's amazing, and it's honestly chilling in a nice way.

As a reader, I'd personally want Blue to be right: that the entire anomaly is just an anomalous divider between the groups. But in reality, it's like Model Red, because otherwise…

But you can't know. No one does. And if Ehwez tries to figure it out, it could spell completely disaster.

The line that best sums this up is this:

We could be sitting on a landmine, or on a cushion, and either way it would really be a poor idea to get up right now.

My only complaint is the Model Blue and Model Red coloring in the object class is a bit unfriendly (the rest of the colored text has context). I'd add a small footnote to the Object Class, but that's it.

Good job!

item.title: Re: I'd Rather Be Part of the Serpent's Hand Than the Foundation"
item.content:encoded:
I've thought about this several times, and I could never be loyal to the SCP Foundation as it stands in-universe. The Foundation commits human rights violations without a second thought at every turn, even when completely unnecessary, and their fundamental approach to the anomalous is flawed. For every -EX, there are a dozen "unexplained" anomalies which are totally understood by the Foundation's understanding of science and could easily be added to current sciences. Memetics, the multiverse, and SCP-439 jump to mind pretty quickly.

item.title: Re: The ANTECHAMBER: SCP seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for reviewing my concept. I was aware that a few SCPs dealt with Christian-like concepts of Hell, though I had not seen SCP-4661 or Arcadia.

My plan was to use a detached, clinical tone in Containment Procedures and Description, and then to use a slightly more narrative, direct style in a string of Exploration Logs, Interviews, and Incident Reports.

The SCP would include descriptions of how MTFs dealt with manifesting demons (I was being facetious with the "badass demon-killing"), as well as researchers' notes on these entities. But the main focus would be on the people exploring "Hell" (the Foundation would refer to it as the Abyss.)

Over several interview logs, the Mediums who access the SCP would try to explain what they see. The Mediums, who are of several faiths: Christian, Jewish, Islamic, Hindu, Buddhist; would experience the Abyss in different ways, since it is a metaphysical reality, and the human mind often needs to visualize and familiarize abstract concepts. What the Mediums see is often dark and traumatic, and repeated visits to the Abyss often eat away at their mental health.

Interviewing researchers do find a common theme among the Mediums' varying accounts: the horror of the Abyss is self-imposed. More than a simple torture chamber, the souls and entities within are locked in personal reveries, tortured by their own insanity, loneliness, and self-hatred as they constantly relive horrific fantasies and tear each other apart.

I agree that disturbing visuals alone can't carry an article. The central horror in this article is conceptual; existential. The visuals serve to fully realize that; to turn the scary idea into a tangible nightmare.

I had intended for the SCP itself: the Portals, Virgil Events, and such, to be rather mysterious. Mediums always experience some kind of Lobby or Antechamber. This room is manned by a figure in a white mask, (dubbed SCP-XXXX-A) who guides the visitor to the soul they ask for, and/or lets them explore Hell, but never explains itself. I would be happy to go more into this part of the SCP if you think that would improve the article.

As for the Chaos Insurgency, I only mention it once. A dead spy who had information the Foundation needed was a good motive for it to start using this SCP. Is there a problem in using the Insurgency?

P.S.: Is MTF Psi-8 "Silencers" the right group for this SCP?

item.title: Re: Return to Monke - Greenlight Request / Review
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. I'll admit that the first few sentences of the description make me think of SCP-1836 (Mother in the Ice), only this is kind of a less interesting version because 1836 incorporates the legendary figure Sedna. This iceberg just kind of… seemingly exists in a strangely specific way for no reason.

Over the course of the article, a journal is found from a monkey

This just seems too conveniently story-wise. A lot of readers these days tend to be skeptical of the "wow look how nice that someone left a document that explains everything and also spoonfeeds story exposition too!" approach; if you really want to have the majority of the information about the item come from the documentation, a tale or GoI-format document may be a better approach. Otherwise the Foundation involvement seems like an afterthought, which wouldn't make sense for an SCP article about something seemingly so grandiose in terms of human implications.

who was bestowed intelligence by the Avatar of the Earth. Our monkey scientist then grapples with the stupidity of mankind,

I'm confused as to why the monkey scientist is so immediately dismissive of humans. We've got stuff like cloud seeding, painkillers, the internet… it also seems rather hypocritical to just see humans as a whole as "stupid" given that there are plenty of intelligent and good-hearted people out there.

before realizing that the only way to protect what gave him the ground to stand on, is to pack everything away and create a failsafe, so that Earth may live on.

I'm not sure what this means. What is the failsafe? What is being packed away? And if the monkey thinks humans are so stupid, why bother writing a journal that humans can understand?

Sorry, but I don't see this being workable at its current stage because all the individual elements seem kind of haphazardly smashed together rather than being thematically related in the context of the story. How is an iceberg related to turning people into monkeys, and how is that related to some random scientist dishing out their hot take on humanity? Why are shrines with feeling-language needed at all in this story?

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: The Necro-Matriarch Broadcast Manifestations
item.content:encoded:
For the ones who have a bad memory, no matter how severe it is, that same "grandma" will be completely different.

As for the language barrier problem, It will be no worry since the anomaly would be able to speak their language at ease, due to you know, them having an innate knowledge of the subject's past and current life.

Yeah, both of these make me as a reader skeptical because it just makes the anomaly too perfect and helpful, which comes off more as artificial and disingenuous to me as a reader rather than heartwarming.

+ show block
– hide block

I am sorry, I didn’t quite catch that. Could you please elaborate it?

What is the reason in the Foundation universe world for the radio to do what it does? Did someone make it because they wanted to talk to their grandma? Is a ghost grandma living in the radiowaves to haunt them? Some other reason?

I am planning to make “convenient online post” to be like the debut of the anomaly in the Foundation’s eyes

My point is that this is a kind of boring initial investigation setup.

Almost as if the mysterious creator of this anomaly is trying to play games with the Foundation, and benefit them at the same time.

Why would the creator want to play games with the Foundation?

On a unrelated note, do antique radios still function normally like they do, because I thought they were just for display.

I'm not familiar with antique radios. Although, if it only affects such radios, would there really be that many people who would be affected by such an anomaly, to the point where the Foundation would have enough cases to notice?

I only written the increased percentage in the draft, in about 35.5 percent.

I'm not sure a qualitative value like "morale" would be readily quantifiable or understandable when presented as a percentage. I recommend just sticking to similarly qualitative descriptions. There's no need to force a random percentage into the writing, especially given that readers will interpret percentages differently (one person might think 35.5 is a lot statistically, another person might think it's a number too small to be worth mentioning in a report).

The last thing you said is also great for a possible Tale about this skip

I personally am not convinced you'd be able to make a tale for this—the material I've mentioned would make more sense for a log or supplement page. Focus on writing an SCP article first.

item.title: Re: The Hinterland Division (How many apocalypses could there be?)
item.content:encoded:
Okay so let me try to explain it a little bit better since my original post was kind of vague. The division technically already existed and has been a key part of the foundation since not long after the Foundations conception, and has already eliminated several threats. The foundation isn’t really making a new division this is just a story behind the creation of the newest iteration of its leader. The reason that the other divisions of the foundation are not sufficient at it is because the threats that the division is made to stop are those that require entire knowledge of the foundation and it’s recourses , regardless of the security needed to have that information. The main idea of the story is very much inspired by the book Enders Game, I’m not sure if you’ve read it. The idea is that the existing Hinterland division is failing because it has not had someone fulfilling the position of the leader and strategist in years, as no good candidates have been found, and without someone that has the prowess to spearhead the division the researchers and members in the division are struggling to do it. The agent that the O5 chooses is purposefully trained and manipulated into being the best possible person to continue the work of the division. This story isn’t really meant to create a new part of the foundation but to explore an existing part of it that has been in my head for a really long time but is not included in any records due to the importance of its mission making its secrecy extremely important as well. I really want to shed some light and provide a look into what’s behind the curtain of the foundation since once you reach the level of the O5 and their staff everything gets rather hazy. The main character is of course the most explored and shown character but he also has several people he knows within the foundation, and I plan to actually develop the character at least partially of one of the O5 members, the one that is currently fulfilling the role of O5-13. There are going to be tales that show characters a low in the foundation of D class personnel in all of this as well. Of course I’m probably not going to write everything about this idea I’m coming up with as this is technically part of an even larger story about how the foundation has been changing and events within it over the years, this is just my version of a snippet of the mysteries in the ever mysterious organization.

item.title: Re: SCP IDEA: "Home"
item.content:encoded:
Sorry about the wait,

I didn't intend to make it sound like the village had ties to the Sarkic Cults. I meant that the SCP Foundation thought that the village had ties to the Sarkic Cults because of the flesh creatures. The members of the village, before anyone enters, are featureless flesh like creatures. There are animals that roam around the village that are also featureless. Once someone enters the village, the animals will resemble animals familiar to the person, such as their childhood dog.

I've decided that the village used to be a commune that a person stumbled upon one day. The commune was dwindling on supplies but tried to hide that fact. The person joins the commune after a while and feels at home. One day, the members of the commune attacked him, burned him, and ate him. They were planning on doing this the whole time and they gave him a false sense of home. This person was somehow anomalous and didn't know it, their soul combined with the village and terrorized the people living in it. The village now wants to bring the same fate to all who come across it in a fit of rage. It plays off of nostalgia because it has decided thats the best way to make people feel at home.

item.title: Mothers Know Best
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Short description with a series of logs that relate multiple unconnected cases

Elevator Pitch: Parasitic worms that have the appearance of elongated human fetuses. They emerge from the wombs of mothers undetected and attach themselves to the mother's (adult) offspring like a leech. Using memetic camouflage to avoid detection, they begin mutating the host's biology and psychology in order to transform them into forms that would please the mother most. They then feed off of the resultant affection given to the host by the mother.

Narrative etc here
wow there it is

Central Narrative: There are three cases logged. In one, a conservative mother estranged from her trans daughter is delighted when the parasite begins to cause the daughter to "de-transition." When the Foundation contains the subject and removes the parasite, the daughter returns to normal. (disclaimer: it is not lost on me that this is a sensitive topic. As a trans individual myself, it is my intention to play on the horror of a transphobic mother/daughter relationship, and not to merely act out conversion therapy.)

In the second, shortest log, a child in a healthy relationship with the mother is infected, but the parasite shrivels and dies, unable to increase its intake of affection because the mother is happy with her child as they are.

In the third, a parasite manifests in an extremely (but subtly) abusive relationship in which the mother exhibits masked hostility towards her child. The parasite, unable to find a form that would please the mother, mutates the host in bizarre ways before bringing them to the brink of death, implying that the only scenario that would please this mother is the near-death of her child. The Foundation recovers the parasite, resuscitates the victim, and re-homes them away from their mother.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A parasite that horrifies readers not only with biological manipulation, but also by visibly manifesting the toxic consequences of abusive expectations for adult children. Imagine if you were forced against your will to please your mother. Not a scenario I'd relish, as much as I love my mom.

Additional Notes: I think this piece will live or die on the effectiveness of the case logs. How can I best insure that these land? Are they the best way to explore this particular topic?

item.title: Re: The Chaos Insurgency is dead. Long live the Chaos Insurgency.
item.content:encoded:
Sure thing, I was craving for answering this (but couldn't before due to space constraints).

Collapsible so Zyn doesn't come suplexing me in the name of mobile users
– hide block

Anyway, for the characters, I have (besides the established folks from the ☽☽☽-Initative) nobody who really "stands out" - in fact, the first two folks are literally nameless mooks referred to by their job. Given that I'm constantly perspective swapping, wasting time on fleshing out the on-offs too much would harm the narrative, imho.

The first "scene" covers how the Insurgency acquired knowledge of Corbenic (or atleast the tech to communicate there), in what is essentially "reframing Dr. Spiegels death in a car crash as assassination ploy" (hopefully daveyoufool will be okay with that).

After that I want to jump directly into the 5000-Action, with the Insurgency being decimated before they even can react and a last, lethaly wound insurgent using his last moments to send out a "message in a bottle" - I'm a huge fan of "contigency plans withing contigency plans", and this is pretty much where the gears start turning.

The rest of the story plays within Corbenic during the plot of Why? unfolding (e.g. 2020-01-02 to 2020-04-121).

Knowing that the Initiative could crush them with ease, the Insurgency resorts to multiple nonviolent resistance methods to face them.

This includes simple civil disobediance against the Initiative (just imagine the distrust a single charismatic leader can spark amongst the huge influx of new-quietus2) up to full blown agitprop campaigns against the Initiative. (Afterall, they have intervened in the past - what justification do they have to ignore this event?)

Eventually, a great mass of Insurgents will just peacefully turn themselves in to the authorities - not the new-quietus though, but older Insurgents, some of them former double-agents that undercut the Initiative. This does not just causes chaos, but is also their ultimate threat: they have given up their covers themselves; nobody knows how many of them are still amidst them.3

All together, they can even pressure the Initiative in hearing them in an attempt to buy time whilst trying to figure out who coordinates4 the Insurgency, and stopping them.

In the end… their efforts were in vain, probably. Because as we all know, project PNEUMA never happened and they got nowhere before it "un-happened". I don't want to ruin the really good ending of SCP-5000, so trying to keep the ambigous ending both bittersweet but also deeply disturbing (from the perspective of the afterlife) might be in need for critique the most later on.

Footnotes
1. Pls tell me if I got the dates wrong. [Insert grumbling over date formats here.]
2. ☽☽☽-speak for "people who just died and wander Corbenic naked and confused". I made it up in another work of mine and its english translation, and now refuse to let go of it. Sorry.
3. This assumes the Initiative is incapable to background check everyone in Corbenic - given that everyone who ever died in the multiverse ends up their, perhaps believable. If not, cut me some slack and assume they were undercover at the Foundation of GOC before and thusly enthusiastically recruited.
4. Just in case you wonder - the Insurgency has AIs too ^^

item.title: Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Siners
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator pitch: A Book made by God (I presume) or Peter Binsfeld to test humans of their sins. If an individual fails the test they will be tortured by the biblical being assigned to that certain sin and have their face and name burned into the pages of the book forever trapped in eternity.

Central narrative: It first sets the focus on the possible origin of the book and then the trial runs itself. If an individual opens the book and begins to read it they fall into a trance and are unable to move. Note that the individual must have to book in its hands or else no words will appear for the person. It is to note that only for the person holding the book the text appears. At next, the trial runs for each of the sins begin which I need to figure out as well to make it accurate according to the sin itself. This will also go in order and after each passed test it gets harder and harder (by that I mean that the order in which the sins will be tested goes from "weakest" sin to "strongest" in terms of passing). Ultimately if an individual fails to pass a test the icon of the according sin will appear and torture the human. Their name and face will be burned into the last pages of the book (which can be read by anyone without any fear of getting trapped) and along the sin which they failed to overcome including their torture. Their soul is therefore trapped inside the book unable to escape leaving the body to show signs of their horrible torture.

Hook, attention grabber: I think it is very interesting to maybe learn about the different trial runs of certain humans with their backstory and also give a hint or two about the price of passing all the tests by the sins. But ultimately there will be no human to this date who has passed the test…or maybe their will but that I would still need to plan and think about.

item.title: Emergency broadcast system from space.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Sci-fi

Page Layout (Optional): normal

Elevator Pitch: The foundation periodically intercepts an audio signal from space, specifically somewhere in the Andromeda constellation, that can be understood by everyone, no matter what language the person speaks. the foundation is unable to recreate the message. The message warns, that there has been an unknown accident in a place outside the milky way. Its suggested, that some sort of anomalous system has failed and potentially released an anomalous entity

Central Narrative: The signal was first intercepted in 2012, by a small team of scientists. One of them was from the foundation. He alerted the foundation and it overtook the research of the signal and the rest of the scientits, that originally found it were amnesticized. The signal periodically gets intercepted biyearly. That makes 4 signals, each would be documented in the article, showing the progression of the event. First one - Announcment of the start of the event. Second - Progression of the event. Third - Dangerous development of the event. Fourth - Progress report on the event. In the end, the foundation waits for the next signal in 2022.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the hook would be the idea of an emergency broadcast intercepted from an alien race, that has a Foundation, similar to the SCP Foundation and of course also the mystery of the event and following along how it develops.

Additional Notes: This would be my first article.

Hey Peppertoast,
first or all, I'd like to say that this skip is a nice little gem, short but descriptive and interesting. I think I'm still missing something, but I believe most of the following is true.

+ show block
– hide block


So, at first I was looking at various obscure numerology things with the numbers of every deer, the number 22, the ages of the Gilmor family and so on.

Then, with the hint of the EXPLOSIONS theme, I looked at the date of the "displacement", 15th May 1955, which at first I thought was simply a reference to the SCP number. By looking up the events on that date, it turns out that on that date took place the last nuclear Test of the so-called "Operation Teapot", right there in Nevada, code name "Zucchini".

So, my current idea is the following: in the Gilmor family there was one (or more) reality benders, and that jolly bunch got (for whatever reason), caught by the Zucchini nuclear explosion: this prompted the reality bender to save its family by creating this weird "Semantic Dimension", which interacts with the baseline in ways both physical and purely semantic, such as the huge amount of zucchini being a transposition of the devastating energy of the zucchini explosion. This semantic connection is extended to all of the house, the things that are inside and its inhabitants. I'm not entirely sure of this, but I suspect that the connections we see are the following:
- Deer 19: Brisbane (btw, Euridyce because she wants to come back from the death and is the only one aware? Nice)
- Deer 21: Rhonda, who's cooking something (Deer 09 & Deer 16, and given the end of the log also Deer 03) by first cutting it and then cooking it (through the oven, which is Deer 01?)
- Deer 07: Sassafras, who runs with Brisbane?
- Deer 14: Suzie
- Deer 04: Edward, with Suzie on his shoulders
- Deer 22: not sure at all. The handle of Deer 01/the oven?

Lastly, so, who's the reality bender? My initial guess was Brisbane, as she's the only one aware and she's in all this biblical frenzy trying to resurrect Jesus, but really I believe it's Edward. He's the one asking what happens to a God/RB when he dies (which is, their fate), he's the one that regrets putting Suzie in this dimension, and he's the one who's 33 years old. Maybe Brisbane got the father's gift and is figuring out how to use it to try to resurrect Jesus/the father from this dimension, don't know. Not even sure if the number 22 and the Deer ones mean anything, would like to know at this point.

So yeah, maybe I'm completely off, but I suspect at least the general idea is there. Let me know Peppermint, and again sincere compliments for the beautiful skip.

item.title: The chocolate man. Seeking a greenlight / feedback on idea.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Genre: Emotional with a pinch of mystery.

Elevator pitch: Without the backstory, it is just a chocolate statue that can only move if a room is at or above the melting point of chocolate and any human it touches is transformed into a blob of chocolate that can sprout hundreds of little leg-like appendages to move around at any temperature above -10 degrees celsius.

Central narrative: It follows a baker who has suffered the loss of some of his loved ones. To cope, he recreated his deceased brother out of chocolate. Then a group of cultists approach him and offer to bring it to life, for a price. He graciously accepts the offer and the cultists perform a ritual to bring the statue to life. The baker asks what the price is and the cultits tell him he will see. The price was that anyone the statue came into contact with would turn into chocolate. The Foundation contained it and brought the baker in for an interview. During the interview, as he starts to explain how the cultists brought it to life, he enters a state of paranoia and gets out of the interview room, he is later found and terminated.

Hook, attention grabber: I think the story that is expressed through the baker will make the reader feel a sense of empathy for him, considering he has lost many loved ones. And I think that the few parts that are redacted will leave the reader wanting more.

SCP-5168-2 appears to be the human male Private Mas Philip moulded with a carbon fibre-like material. Now labelled SCP-5168-1. SCP-5168-2 is 187m tall just as Private Maz was. Private Mas Philip was a former member of MTF Nu-7 ”Hammer Down” infantry force.

scp-5057 (The Secret Ingredient Is Mayo) by YummyBees deleted at -13 and three votes.

SCP-5057 is a ██████████ brand chocolate cake. Anomalous effects occur when a subject makes contact with the cake. The subject will be instantly transported to a child's birthday party in an alternate world, however, details vary between reports.

Feedback ported:

[+] from Quicksilvers
– hide block

+1 from me, simple and strange! Just a few things could be fixed up, though!

(he shifts nervously in his seat)

Usually when subjects do an action during an interview/recorded file, its italicized and is its own line. Here's an example from 4018:

PoI-4018-0: I know how easy it is to pretend that the old pretenses and euphemisms still hold up, and that people take the easy route when confronting things head on is hard. So I'm sorry for making things that much harder to cope with. But really, you know I had to do it to them.

PoI-4018-0 tosses a lit lighter onto the ground, igniting the gasoline. The fire spreads towards the recruitment center; shortly after it reaches the interior, the building goes up in flames.

PoI-4018-0: If I'm pissing you off, or…

Also, the other thing is this sentence:

The subject will be instantly transported to an alternate world which varies between subjects, however it is always a child's birthday party and a ██████████ chocolate cake is always being served.

"…it is always a child's birthday party" doesn't really fit the rest of the sentence (weird syntax) and maybe should be rewritten or reworded. The dialogue in the interview also seems a little stiff.

Sorry if I dumped a little too much crit - I just like the idea and it needs a little tweaking for it to shine more!

The piece is well written and it took me two reads, spaced by more than a year, to reach a conclusion, but ultimately it was a downvote.

Several aspects helped in this decision, but most boil down to the pathos of the piece being predicated on the Christianity of all the involved, including the reader. On the last tab it works, the drama of the character marries well with the piece, but on the rest of the article?

If it were write in such a way to convey the horror of someone loosing their own faith regardless, or if the punch were on the potential consequences of such a crude rewrite on history, maybe that would be another thing, but for me this is too much based on being scary for Christians for theological reasons.
